morning_starts.title: Joe's Bakery & Coffee Shop
morning_starts.note: East Austin's family-run breakfast altar — migas and pan dulce like abuela ran the griddle.

morning_starts.title: Comadre Panadería
morning_starts.note: Conchas that put the corner-store version to shame — get there before the tray's empty.

morning_starts.title: Veracruz All Natural
morning_starts.note: The migas taco that launched a thousand mornings — worth the truck line, always.

morning_starts.title: Houndstooth Coffee
morning_starts.note: Careful pour-over and zero attitude — exactly how a slow Austin morning should read.

morning_starts.title: Merit Coffee
morning_starts.note: Clean, bright cup for folks who take the beans seriously without the fuss.

morning_starts.title: Rockman Coffee + Bakeshop
morning_starts.note: Fresh bake and a solid espresso — a low-key start away from the crowds.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Barton Springs Pool
beach_lake_outdoor.note: 68 degrees year-round, spring-fed and sacred — the coldest, best cure for a Texas summer.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Ann and Roy Butler Hike-and-Bike Trail & Boardwalk
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Ten miles around Lady Bird Lake with the skyline for company — Austin's living room.
beach_lake_outdoor.business: Ann and Roy Butler Hike-and-Bike Trail & Boardwalk

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Congress Avenue Bridge Bats
beach_lake_outdoor.note: 1.5 million bats spiral out at dusk — the best free show in town, hands down.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Barton Creek Greenbelt
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Limestone swimming holes and shaded trail — the wild heart hiding right in the city.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Rowing Dock
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Grab a paddleboard or kayak and float the lake — heat honesty says do it early.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Mount Bonnell (Covert Park)
beach_lake_outdoor.note: A short climb to the best sunset over the river — bring somebody you like.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: McKinney Falls State Park
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Waterfalls and swimming holes minutes from downtown — proof the Hill Country starts here.

culture_history.title: Bullock Texas State History Museum
culture_history.note: The whole Texas story under one roof — start here to understand why we're weird.

culture_history.title: LBJ Presidential Library
culture_history.note: Ten floors of the man who shaped a century — the animatronic LBJ tells a joke.

culture_history.title: Texas State Capitol
culture_history.note: Taller than the one in D.C. on purpose — free tours and pink granite pride.

culture_history.title: Blanton Museum of Art
culture_history.note: Ellsworth Kelly's glowing chapel alone is worth the trip — and it's a bargain.

culture_history.title: The Historic Victory Grill
culture_history.note: Chitlin' Circuit royalty on East 11th — the soul of Black Austin still standing.

culture_history.title: Mexic-Arte Museum
culture_history.note: Downtown home for Mexican and Latino art — the culture that built this city.

culture_history.title: The Contemporary Austin - Laguna Gloria
culture_history.note: Sculpture in the trees on a lakeside villa grounds — art you wander through.

shopping_browsing.title: Waterloo Records
shopping_browsing.note: The record store that defines Austin listening — in-store shows and vinyl for days.

shopping_browsing.title: BookPeople
shopping_browsing.note: Texas's biggest independent bookstore — two floors of getting happily lost.

shopping_browsing.title: Allens Boots
shopping_browsing.note: A wall of cowboy boots on South Congress — try a pair on even if you don't buy.

shopping_browsing.title: Uncommon Objects
shopping_browsing.note: Curated oddities and antiques — the keep-it-weird spirit distilled into a storefront.

shopping_browsing.title: Antone's Record Shop
shopping_browsing.note: Blues on the shelves since '87 — dig with the ghosts of the greats.

shopping_browsing.title: Feathers Boutique Vintage
shopping_browsing.note: Hand-picked vintage threads on the East Side — where the good stuff hides.

shopping_browsing.title: STAG Provisions for Men
shopping_browsing.note: Rugged, well-made menswear with a Texas backbone — quality that lasts.

casual_lunch.title: Franklin Barbecue
casual_lunch.note: The brisket the whole world lines up for — get in line early, it's a pilgrimage.

casual_lunch.title: Terry Black's Barbecue
casual_lunch.note: Family pit-smoked and no reservation-to-brisket wait — a fast lane to the good stuff.

casual_lunch.title: Veracruz All Natural
casual_lunch.note: Beyond breakfast — the tacos hold up all day and the salsa's serious.

casual_lunch.title: Home Slice Pizza
casual_lunch.note: New York slices on South Congress — the easy, no-fuss midday move.

casual_lunch.title: Matt's El Rancho
casual_lunch.note: Tex-Mex since 1952 and the Bob Armstrong dip — comfort with a history.

casual_lunch.title: Nixta Taqueria
casual_lunch.note: East Side tacos reinventing the masa game — the duck carnitas is the one.

casual_lunch.title: Loro Asian Smokehouse & Bar
casual_lunch.note: Smoked-meat-meets-Southeast-Asia from Uchi's brains — the smoked brisket rice is a lunch winner.

happy_hour_drinks.title: The Roosevelt Room
happy_hour_drinks.note: Serious cocktails from folks who competed for the title — every era on one menu.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Small Victory
happy_hour_drinks.note: A tucked-away cocktail room downtown — quiet, well-made, and worth finding.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Zilker Brewing Company
happy_hour_drinks.note: East Side neighborhood brewery — pull up to the taproom and stay a while.

happy_hour_drinks.title: The Austin Beer Garden Brewing Company (ABGB)
happy_hour_drinks.note: Award-winning beer, wood-fired pizza, live music — the trifecta done right.
happy_hour_drinks.business: The Austin Beer Garden Brewing Company (ABGB)

happy_hour_drinks.title: Deep Eddy Cabaret
happy_hour_drinks.note: A proper old Austin dive — cheap, unpretentious, exactly the point.

happy_hour_drinks.title: LoLo
happy_hour_drinks.note: Natural wine and small plates on the East Side — the low-lit spot to linger.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Half Step
happy_hour_drinks.note: Rainey Street cocktails on a patio built for it — go before the crowd swells.

dinner_casual.title: Banger's Sausage House & Beer Garden
dinner_casual.note: Endless sausage links and taps on Rainey — a rowdy, easy Austin night.

dinner_casual.title: Loro Asian Smokehouse & Bar
dinner_casual.note: Smoke and spice in a lively room — perfect low-stakes group dinner.

dinner_casual.title: Odd Duck
dinner_casual.note: Farm-driven small plates that started as a food trailer — inventive without the stiffness.

dinner_casual.title: Canje
dinner_casual.note: Caribbean fire and rum on the East Side — bright, bold, and a whole lot of fun.

dinner_casual.title: Güero's Taco Bar
dinner_casual.note: South Congress Tex-Mex institution with live music out back — a classic hang.

dinner_casual.title: Home Slice Pizza
dinner_casual.note: Slices and pitchers, no reservation needed — the reliable weeknight answer.

dinner_casual.title: Matt's El Rancho
dinner_casual.note: Generations-deep Tex-Mex and frozen margaritas — dinner that feels like family.

dinner_upscale.title: Uchi
dinner_upscale.note: Tyson Cole's sushi temple that put Austin on the fine-dining map — book ahead.

dinner_upscale.title: Hestia
dinner_upscale.note: Live-fire cooking around a wood hearth — precise, dramatic, and delicious.

dinner_upscale.title: Jeffrey's
dinner_upscale.note: Old-guard Clarksville elegance — the tableside martini cart is a whole occasion.

dinner_upscale.title: Lutie's Garden Restaurant
dinner_upscale.note: Garden-set fine dining at Commodore Perry — a splurge that earns every dollar.

dinner_upscale.title: Emmer & Rye
dinner_upscale.note: Dim-sum-cart tasting of hyper-seasonal plates and house grains — a rolling adventure.

dinner_upscale.title: Barley Swine
dinner_upscale.note: Ambitious tasting menu from Odd Duck's kin — the chef's-counter seat is the move.

dinner_romantic.title: Este
dinner_romantic.note: Coastal Mexican seafood with a raw bar glow — order the tuna tostada and share.

dinner_romantic.title: Suerte
dinner_romantic.note: Masa magic and mezcal on the East Side — candlelit and quietly one of the best.

dinner_romantic.title: Comedor
dinner_romantic.note: Modern Mexican in a stunning downtown room — the kind of dinner you remember.

dinner_romantic.title: Birdie's
dinner_romantic.note: Wine-bar seasonal plates in a golden-hour patio setting — small, charming, beloved.

dinner_romantic.title: Bufalina
dinner_romantic.note: Neapolitan pizza and a thoughtful natural wine list — intimate and unhurried.

dinner_romantic.title: Uchi
dinner_romantic.note: Omakase in low light — hand somebody the reins and let the kitchen court you both.

nightlife.title: The White Horse
nightlife.note: Honky-tonk two-steppin' and cheap beer on the East Side — free dance lessons, no cover attitude.

nightlife.title: The Continental Club
nightlife.note: The soul of South Congress since 1955 — live music every night in a room that's seen it all.

nightlife.title: Antone's Nightclub
nightlife.note: Austin's home of the blues — the room where legends were made and still play.

nightlife.title: The Mean Eyed Cat
nightlife.note: A tiny Johnny Cash shrine of a dive — strong pours and no pretense.

nightlife.title: Mohawk
nightlife.note: Red River's beloved rock club — the tiered patio stage is a rite of passage.

nightlife.title: The Broken Spoke
nightlife.note: The last of the true Texas dance halls — chicken-fried steak then waltz across the floor.

nightlife.title: Half Step
nightlife.note: Rainey Street cocktails and a courtyard that hums late — a smooth nightcap stop.

family_activities.title: Zilker Botanical Garden
family_activities.note: Koi ponds, a dinosaur trail, and quiet paths — easy joy for every age.

family_activities.title: Congress Avenue Bridge Bats
family_activities.note: The free bat show at dusk — kids lose their minds and it costs nothing.

family_activities.title: Lone Star Riverboat
family_activities.note: A gentle paddlewheel cruise on Lady Bird Lake — bats and skyline from the water.

family_activities.title: UMLAUF Sculpture Garden & Museum
family_activities.note: Bronze sculpture on shaded lawns — room for little legs to roam.

family_activities.title: Zilker Park Boat Rentals
family_activities.note: Pedal boats and kayaks the whole crew can pile into — simple on-water fun.

family_activities.title: Home Slice Pizza
family_activities.note: Slices that keep everybody happy — the no-drama family dinner spot.

family_activities.title: Q2 Stadium (Austin FC)
family_activities.note: Verde-clad soccer nights that feel like a citywide block party — bring the kids.

rainy_day.title: Blanton Museum of Art
rainy_day.note: Ellsworth Kelly's chapel glows brightest under gray skies — a dry, beautiful refuge.

rainy_day.title: Bullock Texas State History Museum
rainy_day.note: Three floors of Texas plus an IMAX — wait out the storm learning something.

rainy_day.title: Mexic-Arte Museum
rainy_day.note: Downtown and dry, packed with vivid Mexican and Latino art — an easy duck-inside.

rainy_day.title: BookPeople
rainy_day.note: Two floors to browse away a downpour — the coziest place in town when it rains.

rainy_day.title: Paramount Theatre
rainy_day.note: A restored 1915 movie palace — catch a classic film or a show and forget the weather.

rainy_day.title: LBJ Presidential Library
rainy_day.note: Ten dry floors of history — the storm outside is nothing next to the ones inside.

rainy_day.title: Waterloo Records
rainy_day.note: Flip through vinyl and catch an in-store set — a rainy afternoon well spent.
